title: AuthN, AuthZ, Encryption & Secrets
summary: Authentication establishes identity; authorization decides permissions; encryption protects data in transit and at rest; secrets management prevents credential sprawl. System designs that bolt these on late leak.

sections.title: AuthN patterns
paragraphs: Sessions, JWTs, mTLS for service identity, OAuth/OIDC for delegated user login. Know token lifetime, revocation, and audience restrictions.

sections.title: AuthZ models
paragraphs: RBAC, ABAC, ReBAC. Enforce on every data path — UI checks are not security. Central policy engines help, but local enforcement must fail closed.

sections.title: Encryption
paragraphs: TLS everywhere in transit. At rest: disk encryption plus field-level for sensitive columns. Key rotation and envelope encryption are part of the design.

sections.title: Secrets
paragraphs: No secrets in images or git. Use a vault/KMS with short-lived credentials. Audit access. Rotate on incident without redeploying everywhere.

deepDive.title: AuthN, AuthZ, Encryption & Secrets — Operations
paragraphs: Operating AuthN, AuthZ, Encryption & Secrets in production means defining SLIs before tuning knobs, knowing amplification costs, and rehearsing failure modes.
Prefer reversible changes, feature flags, and canaries. Measure p50/p99 and error rate under load that matches production skew.
bullets: Define capacity from the scarcest resource
Keep rollback cheaper than forward repair when possible

deepDive.title: AuthN, AuthZ, Encryption & Secrets — Failure modes
paragraphs: Common failures around AuthN, AuthZ, Encryption & Secrets include overload, partial dependency outages, and silent correctness bugs that pass happy-path tests.
Inject faults in staging: latency, loss, clock skew, and disk full. Verify alerts fire and degradation is intentional.

expert.title: AuthN, AuthZ, Encryption & Secrets — Expert notes
paragraphs: At the expert level, AuthN, AuthZ, Encryption & Secrets intersects multi-region consistency, cost envelopes, and organizational constraints (team ownership, on-call load).
Write down the non-goals. Many outages come from optimizing a metric that was never the product requirement.
